record.paper_title: Current Open Questions in Complete Mixability
record.original_question: Given positive numbers a_{i,j} representing the time taken by worker (i, j) to complete production step j, and using permutations σ_1, …, σ_n ∈ S_m to assign one worker from each step to each of m equipments, minimize max_{i=1,…,m} ∑_{j=1}^n a_{σ_j(i),j}. What assignment of workers is optimal, and how can an optimal assignment be computed?

evidence.quote: Here we have two general questions: (i) What is an optimal arrangement (σ_1, . . . , σ_n) for (1)? How could we calculate an optimal arrangement (σ_1, . . . , σ_n)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let m, n be positive integers, and let A = (a_{i,j}) be an m × n matrix with strictly positive real entries; the entry a_{i,j} represents the time required by worker i to perform production step j. There are m identical pieces of equipment, and for each step j ∈ {1, …, n} an assignment σ_j ∈ S_m (the symmetric group on {1, …, m}) is chosen, which assigns the worker σ_j(i) to equipment i for step j. The total processing time on equipment i is

  T_i(σ_1, …, σ_n) = Σ_{j=1}^n a_{σ_j(i), j},

and the makespan is M(σ_1, …, σ_n) = max_{1 ≤ i ≤ m} T_i(σ_1, …, σ_n).

(a) Characterize the tuples (σ_1, …, σ_n) ∈ (S_m)^n that minimize M(σ_1, …, σ_n).

(b) Provide an algorithm that computes such an optimal tuple, and analyze its computational complexity (in particular, determine whether the problem can be solved in time polynomial in m and n, or whether it is NP-hard).
artifact.status_search_result: No direct resolution of this minimax permutation-assignment formulation (as posed in the context of complete mixability) was located. The problem is closely related to multiprocessor scheduling makespan minimization with column-permutation structure, which in general is NP-hard, but a dedicated optimal-arrangement characterization for this exact formulation does not appear to have been published. Status remains best described as open.

status_evidence.title: Assignment problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The assignment problem consists of finding a matching of minimum (or maximum) weight in a weighted bipartite graph; minimax (bottleneck) variants and multi-stage extensions are generally harder.
status_evidence.claim: Standard assignment problem variants are well studied, but the multi-stage minimax variant over n permutations is not covered by classical Hungarian-type algorithms.
